# Personal statement — voice sample (synthetic fixture)

Fictional. Used by the fact-checker recall eval as the supplementary-context
and voice reference.

Most of what pulled me toward logistics was boring on purpose. My first job
out of school was scheduling trucks, and the scheduling tool was a
spreadsheet somebody's manager had built in 2011. Watching dispatchers work
around it taught me more about requirements than any class did.

At Cascade Freight the tracking app was the first thing I owned end to end.
It went well, though not for the reason we planned. We thought people wanted
a map. They wanted a single sentence telling them whether the thing was
late. Rewriting the notification copy did more for support volume than the
map ever did.

Northwind has been a different kind of problem. The carrier-integration work
is unglamorous and it touches real money, so mistakes are expensive and slow
to surface. The automated exception handling is the piece I find most
interesting, though it's in a controlled pilot with a dozen partners and
still in beta, so there isn't much to point at yet.

Outside work it's mostly trail running and a long-running argument with my
sourdough starter.
